reaction.episode: A CORRECTION with no bottom confirmed: SPX closed Friday at 6,910.39, -11.91% from its 120-day high, -9.37% below its 50-day and -5.96% below its 200-day after a -8.61% five-day slide; SMH ($400.06) and NVDA ($125.53) are both below their Zone 2 floors, VIX is 35.89 at its five-day high with no rollover, HY OAS is 3.52 and calm, and the mechanical tally is 1 of 4 — only credit calm confirmed. Data is fresh through Nov 20.
reaction.invalidation: The Watch stance is wrong if SPX closes a week back above its 200-day (7,348.58) with NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 ($175-185) and VIX closing below 25 — or if a confirmed bottom forms first. Either voids this ladder and moves the stance to Probe on the deployment ladder.

ladder.response: No buying — the next zone down is a re-entry map, not a buying level; reassess Tranche C conditions (failed first bounce plus a second low that holds).
ladder.trigger: SPX second weekly close below 7,000, or SMH closing below $400 / NVDA below $120

ladder.response: Do not chase — a failed retest of the failure zone is the bull-trap verdict; entries stay off and the regime-break read is confirmed.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into 7,750-7,820 or SMH into 580-600 and fails there

ladder.response: Stand-down extends and all tranche triggers are void until credit calms and a bottom confirms.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4.00% or VIX holds above 25 with SPX below its 200-day

ladder.response: Tranche A arms on Zone 2 re-occupancy (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185); probe sizing only, no full deployment.
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce plus a second low that holds with the 10-year falling, or a held close above SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600 with the tally at 3 of 4

reaction.trapRisk: The first bounce is the trap: a sharp relief rally into the SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600 failure zone that fails there is the bull-trap case, not a buying opportunity. Entries never chase the first bounce; they wait for the retest verdict — a bounce that fails at the zone confirms the break and keeps new money in bills, while only a held close above the zone, with the tally at 3 of 4, re-arms Tranche A.

strategyPosture: Stand down and watch. SPX is -11.91% from its high and below both its 50- and 200-day lines, SMH and NVDA sit below their Zone 2 floors, VIX is 35.89 with no rollover, and only 1 of 4 mechanical signals is confirmed — there is no bottom to buy yet, so new money stays in bills and no tranche is armed.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking — credit conditions can flip, and a rotation read dies the moment HY OAS breaks 4.00%. Until then, index-level calm masks real weakness in the handful of names that carry the index, and breadth is the tell, not the headline level.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages -24.97% from 52-week highs vs SPY -11.7%, a 13.27-point gap; NVDA is the weakest Mag7 name at -48.4% while AAPL holds at -5.1%. But bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% (SLOOS), far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.52 and calm. The damage is concentrated in the names that dominate the index by weight, not in credit.
themes.label: Mag7 unwind: rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The market reads the Mag7 break as a broad rollover — the index's heaviest names are leading it down, so the whole market must be breaking.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00% or the Mag7-SPY gap widening past 15 points.

themes.counterRead: Sentiment-driven does not mean wrong — price can stay ahead of the turn, and RSI 15 is capitulation, not a buy signal on its own. PLTR, ETN and SNOW carry ACUTE_CATALYST flags, not just sentiment. The gap is an opportunity only with a confirmed bottom; until the episode tally moves, these are watchlist names with promotion conditions, not entries.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue is still growing through the rout: NVDA +61.4% YoY at -48.4% from its high (RSI 15), AVGO +55% at -38.5%, LRCX +131.3% at -58.2%, ONTO +41.5% at -56% with a 29.8% FCF margin, DDOG +27.7% at -47.7% with 80% gross margin, PLTR +91.7% at -32.6%. 27 of 38 dislocations are flagged sentiment-driven, and the conviction screen promotes AVGO, KTOS and ETN at score 80 on recovery-confirmed revenue.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI buildout story is broken — semis and AI suppliers are in freefall, so the demand must be gone.
themes.watchFor: SMH or NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: The fear runs ahead of the credit data — but credit is also the leg that decides whether this stays a correction. The same input that calls credit calm gives it the whole weight of the tally: if HY OAS crosses 4.00%, the rotation read and the re-entry map both change, and the stand-down extends.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.52, flagged calm and not cracking, and it is the only one of four mechanical signals confirmed (tally 1 of 4). The 2s10s curve is +0.28, not inverted. DFF is 3.88. Credit is the one leg of the market that has not broken.
themes.label: Credit calm while equities break
themes.narrative: A -11.91% SPX drawdown with VIX at 35.89 means a credit event is already underway — equities are just the first to show it.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00% — the line where calm becomes cracking.

themes.counterRead: Rates and multiples agree here: at a 5% 10-year, the market pays less per dollar of growth, however real the growth is. The re-rate runs the other way if the 10-year rolls over — but a fast 10-year fall on a growth scare would confirm the scare, not cancel it, so the trigger is the 10-year falling with a bottom confirming, not the yield alone.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is 5.04% and the 30-year 5.40%, with the real 10-year at 2.89%. The input flags AMAT, ROK, KLAC and TER as MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION declines: AMAT is -59.1% from its high while revenue grows +11.4% YoY with a 20.1% FCF margin — a derating, not a business break. The same pattern runs through the semi-cap names.
themes.label: Rates at 5%: the multiple compression
themes.narrative: Growth names should re-rate on their revenue growth — the market is mispricing them.
themes.watchFor: 10-year falling below 5.00% alongside a failed first bounce and a second low that holds.

themes.counterRead: Holding leveraged products through a -8.61% five-day tape is not patience, it is decay — the 'hold and recover' story runs ahead of what the tape supports. These positions need no action tonight and no adding: the re-entry map is written for SMH/NVDA zone re-occupancy, not for averaging down leveraged tickers into a falling tape.
themes.dataAnchor: The leveraged and crypto-linked holdings are the worst of the tape: CONL -65.54% in one month (-11.83% Friday), TQQQ -35.64% (-12.77% Friday), BMNR -40.44% (-11.08% Friday), IBIT -27.59%, BTC -22.53%, ETH -25.13%. QQQ itself is -12.31% in a month, so the 3x products are compounding a falling base with VIX at 35.89.
themes.label: Leveraged holdings: the washout leg
themes.narrative: Leveraged exposure lets you hold through the dip and capture the recovery at a multiple.
themes.watchFor: QQQ reclaiming its 200-day or a confirmed bottom (failed first bounce, second low holding) before any leveraged re-entry is considered.

watchFor: SPX weekly close vs 7,000 — a second close below confirms the regime break; a reclaim of the 200-day at 7,348.58 opens the bounce case.
VIX rollover — VIX closing below 25 after spiking to 35.89, or a lower high after a spike day.
HY OAS closing above 4.00% — currently 3.52 and calm; a cross breaks the credit leg.
SMH/NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) and holding, with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 — the Tranche A arming condition.
PCE Oct on Nov 25, FOMC decision Dec 8-9, CPI Nov on Dec 10 — the three dated catalysts in the active-events list.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the first bounce: either SPX reclaims its 200-day at 7,348.58 and SMH retests the 580-600 failure zone, where the trap verdict is rendered, or the tape escalates down through 7,000 on a second weekly close and confirms the regime break. The trigger is the bounce itself, not a level reached in a straight line down.
